sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey report (group/individual interviews, 160-item wordlists, Kenga recorded-text testing, lexical-similarity percentages). No phonology or orthography section; the only occurrences of 'accent' are questionnaire prompts about villages that speak 'avec un accent' different (regional accent), Annexe A items 1.10-1.11; 'ton', 'tone', 'stress', 'hauteur', 'prosodie' do not occur. Annexe D prints the six 160-item wordlists (Kenga, Naba, Morbo, Bolongue, Bayo, Morom) in broad IPA with vowel length but no tone or stress marking.

sources.note: Nothing. Comparative wordlists collected by Dr Decorse; the author states (p. 174) 'Les transcriptions n'ont aucune précision : toutes les consonnes gardent leur son normal et isolé' and gives only vowel-letter conventions; Gallica full-text search of the whole volume for 'accent', 'tonique', 'intonation' returns 0 hits. Dissa appears only as items in the 'Groupe Barma' comparative vocabulary (pp. ~212-219).
